description: Every prediction case of the prediction spec (revision 27) section 6.5 as calls on the fixture roots, with the hand-written expectations. Generated by conformance/tools/build_fixtures.py; do not edit. Steps with "strict" take their numbers from the reference engine's strict mode (KP1-H writes predict_expected.json); K2b-pin merges both into conformance/cases/predict-*.json.

interface.case: {id, title, spec, root, release, requires, steps, runners?, open_args?, note?}. root is a fixture root (fixtures.json); requires are runner features (K2: predict, localtime_module, localtime, tzdir_env); runners, when present, are the only profiles that run the case (Python-only and not-C cases: there is no feature for them); open_args are matrix.open_args.
interface.matchers: as the conformance cases, plus {$len: n} (an array of n items) and {$from_step: i} (equal to the same field of step i's result); K2b-pin resolves both

results.astro_*: {value} (degrees or a node factor); astro_valid_range {first_year, last_year}. An astro op without id uses release.astro_table() with no id (C: otc_astro_table, then the function on that handle)
results.astro_table: {astro_table: {astro_table_id, v0_model, tables_sha256, generator, first_year, last_year} or null}
results.current_events: as heights, items [{time, type, velocity_ms, direction_deg}]
results.currents: as heights, items [{time, velocity_major_ms, velocity_minor_ms, speed_ms, direction_deg}]
results.datums: {set_id, zero, zero_name, chart_datum, msl_offset_m, levels: [{key, value_m, above_chart_m, kind, method, source_name, epoch, data_span, control_station_id, control_set_id, control_source_id, uncertainty_m, uncertainty_basis, flags}] in key order}; with all_sets: {groups: [that, per set, in file order]}
results.heights, heights_at: {items: [{time, height_m}], station_id, timezone, method, set_id, convention_id, astro_table_id, reference_station_id, reference_bin, datum, datum_name, datum_kind, datum_uncertainty_m, bin_number, omitted_event_types, release, algorithm} (spec 5.3; a field that does not apply is null)
results.ranges: {mn, gt, dhq, dlq}, each null unless both levels have the same kind and epoch
results.to_local: the inner result with tz and tz_version, and local_time and utc_offset_s on every item. step.local.zone is the zone K2b-pin uses to add them to the strict items; step.local.check lists values they must equal

interface.step: {op, args, expect?, expect_if_missing?, strict, local?, swap_of?} or a driver step ({driver: restart_runner, env}) or {op: open, matrix_open} (open the case's root again with open_args changed; null removes one). expect holds the hand-written keys; the numeric items come from strict. An expect with error and a non-null strict is a modelled refusal: the case harness checks that the strict mode raises the same code.

strict.crosscheck: scan_5s (extremes: h'; current events: W' and W), scan_5s_peaks (W' only), scan_5s_slacks (W only): the 5 s brute-force count of spec 6.1 that must equal the event count
strict.entries: webcaltides lib/harmonics_strict.rb (237446c) Engine methods: predict_strict(constituents, times, datum_term:), extremes_strict(constituents, start, stop, datum_term:), currents_strict(bin, times), current_events_strict(bin, start, stop), subordinate_extremes_strict(ref_constituents, chart_datum_term, offsets, start, stop, datum_shift:), subordinate_current_events_strict(ref_bin, offset, start, stop); and two compositions: folded_heights = subordinate_folded_strict(ref_constituents, chart_datum_term, offsets, datum_shift:) then predict_strict on its constituents and datum_term at times; folded_extremes = the same then extremes_strict over start, stop.
strict.references: {$set: set_id} is that set's constituents; {$bin: [set_id, bin]} that bin object; {$offsets: station_id} the station's subordinate_offsets; {$current_offset: [station_id, bin]} that current_offsets entry; astro is the astro_tables entry with that id, passed as astro: Strict::AstroTable.from_h(entry). All in the case's root.

interface.times: ISO 8601 UTC strings YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS(.fff)Z; a naive datetime has no Z (Python only). Result times are whole seconds YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ.
